stem: A binomial variable X has mean 6, and its mean exceeds its variance by 1.8. After recovering its parameters, what is P(X is at least 2), to four decimals?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Computes P(X >= 1) = 1 - P(0) = 1 - 0.7^20 = 0.9992, subtracting only the zero term. 'At least 2' must also remove the P(X = 1) term.
Reports P(X < 2) = P(0) + P(1) = 0.000798 + 0.006839 = 0.0076, the complement of the event asked. This is the probability of fewer than two successes, not at least two.
Reports P(X = 1) = 20(0.3)(0.7)^19 = 0.0068 alone, confusing 'at least 2' with a single exact term. At least two covers X = 2,3,...,20.

explanation: First pin the parameters. Variance = mean - 1.8 = 6 - 1.8 = 4.2. Then q = variance/mean = 4.2/6 = 0.7, so p = 0.3, and n = mean/p = 6/0.3 = 20. 'At least 2' is the complement of the two small tails: P(X >= 2) = 1 - P(0) - P(1) = 1 - 0.7^20 - 20(0.3)(0.7)^19 = 1 - 0.000798 - 0.006839 = 0.9924. The trap is to subtract only P(0); the X = 1 term must also go.

explanation_sections.punchline: Variance = mean - 1.8 = 4.2 unlocks everything: q = variance/mean = 0.7, p = 0.3, n = 20. Then 'at least 2' is 1 minus both the zero and the one term.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: binomial with hidden parameters. Get variance from the offset clue, then variance/mean = q, p = 1 - q, n = mean/p. For at-least-2, subtract the two cheap tail terms P(0) = q^n and P(1) = n p q^(n-1) from 1. The common slip is stopping after P(0); the threshold is 2, so two terms come off.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(X >= k) = 1 - sum of P(0)..P(k-1). For k = 2 you must remove both P(0) and P(1), not P(0) alone.
explanation_sections.timing: About 180 seconds: derive variance, q, p, n, then two power terms and a subtraction. Reject 0.9992 fast, it removes only P(0) and answers at-least-1.
